Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 4.pdf ---
Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT)
So the deal is, we're working with the Defense Biometrics and Forensics folks and NIJ on
this broader contactless fingerprint research effort, and right now nobody has a good way
to actually compare two fingerprint captures side by side and see how much the minutiae
points drift between them. Like, you take a contact scan and a contactless scan of the
same finger, and you want to know objectively how far off the matching ridge features are
from one another — there's just no tool for that today. Researchers are basically eyeballing
it or doing something manual and clunky.
What I'm picturing is a pretty focused little desktop utility, nothing fancy, that lets a
researcher open up a pair of fingerprint files, see the image with all the minutiae points
overlaid on it, and then click on a point on one print and the matching point on the other
print, and the tool just calculates the spatial deviation between them and shows it right
there. They should be able to click into an individual minutia and see its details too — x, y
position, angle, classification, whatever annotations are attached to it.
It'd be nice if on top of that they could filter through the deviations somehow, like mark
pairs as they go, keep a running list during the session, and maybe filter the display based
on some deviation threshold they type in. And being able to export just the minutiae that
pass that filter into a new file would be great too — but honestly that filtering piece is more
of a nice-to-have, if it doesn't make it into the first version that's fine, it's not the core ask.
The core ask really is just the open-compare-calculate flow. Whatever they do during a
session, they need to be able to save it — both as a kind of session file they can reopen
later and pick up where they left off, and as a simple log file, something like a table they
could open in Excel, listing the pairs and the deviations calculated. Everything stays local,
opened and saved from the user's own machine — there's no need for this to talk to any
network or server, that's explicitly not something we want, keep it offline.
Who's going to use this is basically biometrics researchers — academia, government labs,
industry partners — people who already know what they're doing with fingerprint data, so
we don't need to dumb down the interface or build training wheels into it. This isn't a
public-facing product, it's a research instrument that we'll hand out to people who already
understand minutiae and EBTS-type files. Because of that, things like user accounts,
per-user permissions, fancy security layers — none of that matters here, skip it.
One more thing worth flagging: this is very much a prototype/beta-stage tool, not
something we're polishing for general release. It just needs to be stable enough that a
knowledgeable researcher can rely on it without us providing ongoing support afterwards
— once it's out the door, it's pretty much on its own. So let's not over-engineer it, just get
the comparison and measurement piece rock solid first.

Sistema: Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT)

Resumo executivo: The Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT) is an offline desktop prototype for biometrics researchers to objectively compare minutiae from two fingerprint captures of the same finger, including contact and contactless captures. It replaces manual visual comparison by displaying annotated prints, allowing researchers to identify corresponding minutiae, calculating their spatial deviation, and preserving comparison results locally for research analysis.

Escopo: An offline desktop utility that compares minutiae from two locally stored fingerprint files and records their spatial deviations.
  Em escopo: Opening a pair of local fingerprint files, including EBTS-type files [TBD: supported file variants]
  Em escopo: Displaying fingerprint images with minutiae overlays
  Em escopo: Inspecting minutia attributes
  Em escopo: Selecting corresponding minutiae and calculating spatial deviation
  Em escopo: Maintaining a session list of measured pairs
  Em escopo: Saving and reopening local comparison sessions
  Em escopo: Exporting a tabular local deviation log
  Em escopo: Filtering deviations and exporting filtered minutiae
  Fora de escopo: Network, server, cloud, or external-service integration — the tool must operate offline
  Fora de escopo: User accounts and per-user permissions — excluded for the research prototype
  Fora de escopo: Public-facing product capabilities — the tool is intended for qualified researchers
  Fora de escopo: Ongoing post-release support — excluded for the beta-stage delivery
  Fora de escopo: Training workflows or beginner-oriented guidance — target users already understand minutiae and EBTS-type files
  Premissa: PA-01: Researchers provide two fingerprint captures representing the same finger.
  Premissa: PA-02: Input files contain a fingerprint image and associated minutiae data [INFERRED].
  Premissa: PA-03: Researchers manually determine whether two minutiae correspond.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Deployment): The system must be delivered as a desktop utility.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Operation): All file opening, processing, and saving must occur on the user's local machine.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Connectivity): The system must not require network or server communication.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Lifecycle): The system is a prototype/beta-stage research instrument.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Biometrics researcher (Usuário primário): Compare minutiae from two captures objectively, inspect minutia data, calculate deviations, and preserve local research results.
  STK-02 - Defense Biometrics and Forensics stakeholders (Stakeholder externo): Obtain a reliable prototype that supports contactless fingerprint research measurements.
  STK-03 - National Institute of Justice (NIJ) (Stakeholder externo): Support objective analysis of minutiae deviation in the broader contactless fingerprint research effort.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Comparability of captures: A deviation comparison is valid only when the two fingerprint captures represent the same finger.
  RN-002 - Researcher-defined correspondence: A minutia pair is considered corresponding only when a qualified biometrics researcher identifies one minutia in each fingerprint capture as a match.
  RN-003 - Local handling of research data: Fingerprint captures, session data, and deviation results must remain on the researcher's local machine.
  RN-004 - Threshold-based export eligibility: Only minutiae belonging to pairs that satisfy the researcher-entered deviation threshold are eligible for filtered export.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Open fingerprint pair: The system shall open two fingerprint files selected from the user's local machine for a comparison session. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Display minutiae overlays: The system shall display each opened fingerprint image with its available minutiae points overlaid. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Inspect minutia details: The system shall display the x position, y position, angle, classification, and available annotations for a selected minutia. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Select corresponding minutiae: The system shall allow the researcher to designate one minutia from each displayed fingerprint as a corresponding pair. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Calculate spatial deviation: The system shall calculate and display the spatial deviation for a designated corresponding minutia pair. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Maintain deviation list: The system shall add each calculated corresponding pair and its spatial deviation to the current session list. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Mark deviation pair: The system shall allow the researcher to mark an item in the current session deviation list. [Should have]
  RF-008 - Save comparison session: The system shall save the current comparison session to a file selected on the user's local machine. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Reopen comparison session: The system shall restore a previously saved local comparison session from a selected session file. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Export deviation log: The system shall export the current session list as a locally saved tabular log containing each corresponding pair and its calculated spatial deviation. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Filter deviations by threshold: The system shall display only session-list items whose spatial deviation satisfies a researcher-entered threshold. [Could have]
  RF-012 - Export filtered minutiae: The system shall export minutiae belonging to the deviation pairs displayed after threshold filtering into a new local file. [Could have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Functional Suitability) - The system shall calculate spatial deviation with an absolute error no greater than 0.01 pixel against reference coordinate pairs. [TBD: confirm measurement unit and formula] | Métrica: Absolute error of 0.01 pixel or less for 100% of a reference test set. [TBD]
  RNF-002 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall display a calculated deviation within 2 seconds after the researcher designates a corresponding pair. [TBD] | Métrica: 95th-percentile response time of 2 seconds or less across 100 designated-pair calculations. [TBD]
  RNF-003 (Security) - The system shall perform all comparison-session operations with zero outbound network connections. | Métrica: Zero outbound network connections during opening, comparing, saving, reopening, and exporting test sessions.
  RNF-004 (Reliability) - The system shall restore 100% of saved pair records and their deviation values when reopening a valid session file created by the same version. [TBD: define cross-version behavior] | Métrica: 100% record and deviation-value equality in 30 save-and-reopen test sessions. [TBD]
  RNF-005 (Compatibility) - The system shall successfully open 100% of approved EBTS-type sample files containing fingerprint images and minutiae records. [TBD: approve supported EBTS variants] | Métrica: 100% successful opening of the approved sample-file suite, with zero critical parsing errors. [TBD]

Histórias de usuário:
  HU-001 - Como biometrics researcher, quero open two local fingerprint files as one comparison pair, para analyze captures of the same finger side by side
  HU-002 - Como biometrics researcher, quero view each fingerprint with minutiae overlaid, para locate candidate corresponding ridge features
  HU-003 - Como biometrics researcher, quero inspect a selected minutia's attributes, para assess its characteristics before pairing it
  HU-004 - Como biometrics researcher, quero designate two minutiae as corresponding, para measure their positional difference
  HU-005 - Como biometrics researcher, quero see the spatial deviation of a corresponding pair, para obtain an objective comparison measurement
  HU-006 - Como biometrics researcher, quero maintain a list of measured pairs during my session, para review all calculated deviations
  HU-007 - Como biometrics researcher, quero mark a measured pair, para identify it for subsequent review
  HU-008 - Como biometrics researcher, quero save my comparison session locally, para preserve work completed during the session
  HU-009 - Como biometrics researcher, quero reopen a saved comparison session, para continue the analysis from its saved state
  HU-010 - Como biometrics researcher, quero export a tabular deviation log, para analyze the comparison results in spreadsheet software
  HU-011 - Como biometrics researcher, quero filter measured pairs by a deviation threshold, para focus on results meeting my analysis criterion
  HU-012 - Como biometrics researcher, quero export minutiae from filtered pairs, para reuse qualifying results in further research

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Open and display a fingerprint comparison pair | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher selects two local fingerprint files.
    2. The system validates and opens the selected files.
    3. The system displays both fingerprint images with available minutiae overlays.
  UC-002 - Inspect minutia details | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher selects an overlaid minutia point.
    2. The system retrieves the point's available attributes.
    3. The system displays x position, y position, angle, classification, and annotations.
  UC-003 - Measure minutia deviation | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher selects one minutia on the first fingerprint.
    2. The researcher selects one minutia on the second fingerprint.
    3. The system designates the selected minutiae as a corresponding pair.
    4. The system calculates and displays the pair's spatial deviation.
    5. The system adds the pair and deviation to the session list.
  UC-004 - Save and reopen a comparison session | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher selects the save-session action and a local destination.
    2. The system writes the current session to the selected local file.
    3. The researcher later selects a saved session file.
    4. The system restores the saved pair records and deviation values.
  UC-005 - Export deviation results | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher selects the export-log action and a local destination.
    2. The system creates a tabular log containing each session pair and spatial deviation.
    3. The system confirms the created local file path.
  UC-006 - Filter and export qualifying minutiae | Ator: Biometrics researcher
    1. The researcher enters a deviation threshold.
    2. The system displays only pairs satisfying the entered threshold.
    3. The researcher selects an export destination for filtered minutiae.
    4. The system exports minutiae from the displayed qualifying pairs to a new local file.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado that the researcher has two valid local fingerprint files for the same finger, quando the researcher selects both files to start a comparison, então the system shall load exactly two files into the comparison session and display both file names
  CA-002 - Dado that a valid fingerprint pair has been opened, quando the system renders the comparison view, então each displayed fingerprint image shall show every available minutia point from its opened file as an overlay
  CA-003 - Dado that a displayed fingerprint contains a minutia record with x, y, angle, classification, and annotation data, quando the researcher selects its overlaid point, então the system shall display the record's x value, y value, angle, classification, and annotation value
  CA-004 - Dado that two fingerprint images are displayed, quando the researcher selects one minutia on each image and confirms the pairing, então the system shall create one corresponding pair containing exactly the two selected minutiae
  CA-005 - Dado that a designated pair has minutia coordinates (0,0) and (3,4), quando the system calculates the pair's spatial deviation, então the system shall display a spatial deviation of 5.00 pixels [TBD: confirm measurement unit]
  CA-006 - Dado that the session list contains 2 calculated pairs, quando a third corresponding pair is calculated, então the session list shall contain 3 entries, including the third pair and its displayed deviation
  CA-007 - Dado that the session list contains a calculated pair, quando the researcher marks that pair, então the selected session-list item shall display the marked state
  CA-008 - Dado that the current session contains 3 calculated pairs, quando the researcher saves the session to a writable local destination, então the system shall create one session file at the selected path containing 3 pair records
  CA-009 - Dado that a valid local session file contains 3 pair records and their deviation values, quando the researcher opens that session file, então the system shall restore exactly 3 pair records with the same saved deviation values
  CA-010 - Dado that the session list contains 2 calculated pairs, quando the researcher exports the deviation log to a writable local destination, então the system shall create one tabular file containing 2 data rows, each with pair identification and spatial deviation
  CA-011 - Dado that the session list contains deviations of 2.00, 5.00, and 8.00 pixels, quando the researcher enters a threshold of 5.00 pixels, então the system shall display exactly 2 entries with deviations of 2.00 and 5.00 pixels
  CA-012 - Dado that threshold filtering displays exactly 2 qualifying corresponding pairs, quando the researcher exports the filtered minutiae to a writable local destination, então the system shall create one local file containing minutiae from exactly the 2 displayed qualifying pairs

Glossário:
  Minutia: A fingerprint ridge feature represented by positional and descriptive attributes, such as x position, y position, angle, and classification.
  Corresponding pair: Two minutiae, one from each fingerprint capture, identified by a researcher as representing the same ridge feature.
  Spatial deviation: The measured positional difference between the two minutiae in a corresponding pair.
  Contact fingerprint capture: A fingerprint capture acquired through physical contact with a capture surface.
  Contactless fingerprint capture: A fingerprint capture acquired without physical contact with a capture surface.
  EBTS-type file: A fingerprint data file associated with Electronic Biometric Transmission Specification conventions; supported variants are [TBD].
  Comparison session: The locally stored working state containing an opened fingerprint pair, designated pairs, calculated deviations, and marks.

Este documento é a base de conhecimento fixa (Vector Store B) do sistema de elicitação de requisitos. Ele ensina ao agente

Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.
Cadeia de rastreabilidade mínima:
STK → (RN →) RF → HU → CA

A ISO/IEC 25010:2023 define 9 características de qualidade do produto. Todo RNF deve ser 
classificado em uma dessas características. A seguir, cada característica com seus sub-atributos e 
exemplo de RNF.
1. Functional Suitability (Adequação Funcional)
 Functional Completeness — o sistema oferece todas as funções necessárias.
 Functional Correctness — as funções produzem os resultados corretos.
 Functional Appropriateness — as funções facilitam a realização das tarefas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 1. Functional Suitability
O sistema deve calcular o imposto sobre o valor do pedido aplicando corretamente a alíquota de ICMS 
vigente para o estado de destino, conforme tabela oficial CONFAZ, com variação máxima de R$ 0,01 em 
relação ao valor de referência da Receita Estadual.
2. Performance Efficiency (Eficiência de Desempenho)
 Time Behaviour — tempo de resposta e throughput.
 Resource Utilisation — uso de CPU, memória, rede.
 Capacity — limites máximos suportados.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 2. Performance Efficiency
O sistema deve processar no mínimo 200 pedidos por minuto sob carga de 1.000 usuários simultâneos, com 
tempo de resposta inferior a 2 segundos no percentil 95.
3. Compatibility (Compatibilidade)
 Co-existence — coexiste com outros sistemas sem degradação.
 Interoperability — troca dados com outros sistemas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 3. Compatibility

 Appropriateness Recognisability — usuário reconhece a adequação do sistema.
 Learnability — facilidade de aprendizado.
 Operability — facilidade de operação.
 User Error Protection — proteção contra erros do usuário.
 User Engagement — interface envolvente e motivadora.
 Inclusivity — acessível a pessoas com diferentes capacidades.
 User Assistance — suporte ao usuário.
 Self-Descriptiveness — interface autoexplicativa.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 4. Interaction Capability
Um usuário sem treinamento prévio deve ser capaz de registrar seu primeiro pedido completo em até 10 
minutos. A interface deve seguir as diretrizes WCAG 2.1 nível AA.
5. Reliability (Confiabilidade)
 Faultlessness — ausência de falhas em condições normais.

 Fault Tolerance — operação correta mesmo com falhas parciais.
 Recoverability — recuperação após falha.

 Replaceability — substituível por outro produto equivalente.

When old requirements don’t exist
Most older systems do not have documented—let alone accurate—requirements. In the absence of 
reliable documentation, teams might reverse-engineer an understanding of what the system does 
from the user interfaces, code, and database. We think of this as “software archaeology.” To maximize 
the benefit from reverse engineering, the archaeology expedition should record what it learns in 
the form of requirements and design descriptions. Accumulating accurate information about certain 
portions of the current system positions the team to enhance a system with low risk, to replace a 
system without missing critical functionality, and to perform future enhancements efficiently. It halts 
the knowledge drain, so future maintainers better understand the changes that were just made.
If updating the requirements is overly burdensome, it will fall by the wayside as busy people rush 
on to the next change request. Obsolete requirements aren’t helpful for future enhancements. There’s 
a widespread fear in the software industry that writing documentation will consume too much time; 
the knee-jerk reaction is to neglect all opportunities to update requirements documentation. But 
what’s the cost if you don’t update the requirements and a future maintainer (perhaps you!) has to 
regenerate that information? The answer to this question will let you make a thoughtful business 
decision concerning whether to revise the requirements documentation when you change or 
re-create the software.
When the team performs additional enhancements and maintenance over time, it can extend 
these fractional knowledge representations, steadily improving the system documentation. The 
incremental cost of recording this newly found knowledge is small compared with the cost of 
someone having to rediscover it later on. Implementing enhancements almost always necessitates 
further requirements development, so add those new requirements to an existing requirements 
repository, if there is one. If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn 
throughout the project. Try to leave the requirements in better shape than you found them.
Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.

Minutia Deviation Tool (MDT)
So the deal is, we're working with the Defense Biometrics and Forensics folks and NIJ on
this broader contactless fingerprint research effort, and right now nobody has a good way
to actually compare two fingerprint captures side by side and see how much the minutiae
points drift between them. Like, you take a contact scan and a contactless scan of the
same finger, and you want to know objectively how far off the matching ridge features are
from one another — there's just no tool for that today. Researchers are basically eyeballing
it or doing something manual and clunky.
What I'm picturing is a pretty focused little desktop utility, nothing fancy, that lets a
researcher open up a pair of fingerprint files, see the image with all the minutiae points
overlaid on it, and then click on a point on one print and the matching point on the other
print, and the tool just calculates the spatial deviation between them and shows it right
there. They should be able to click into an individual minutia and see its details too — x, y
position, angle, classification, whatever annotations are attached to it.
It'd be nice if on top of that they could filter through the deviations somehow, like mark
pairs as they go, keep a running list during the session, and maybe filter the display based
on some deviation threshold they type in. And being able to export just the minutiae that
pass that filter into a new file would be great too — but honestly that filtering piece is more
of a nice-to-have, if it doesn't make it into the first version that's fine, it's not the core ask.
The core ask really is just the open-compare-calculate flow. Whatever they do during a
session, they need to be able to save it — both as a kind of session file they can reopen
later and pick up where they left off, and as a simple log file, something like a table they
could open in Excel, listing the pairs and the deviations calculated. Everything stays local,
opened and saved from the user's own machine — there's no need for this to talk to any
network or server, that's explicitly not something we want, keep it offline.
Who's going to use this is basically biometrics researchers — academia, government labs,
industry partners — people who already know what they're doing with fingerprint data, so
we don't need to dumb down the interface or build training wheels into it. This isn't a
public-facing product, it's a research instrument that we'll hand out to people who already
understand minutiae and EBTS-type files. Because of that, things like user accounts,
per-user permissions, fancy security layers — none of that matters here, skip it.
One more thing worth flagging: this is very much a prototype/beta-stage tool, not
something we're polishing for general release. It just needs to be stable enough that a
knowledgeable researcher can rely on it without us providing ongoing support afterwards
— once it's out the door, it's pretty much on its own. So let's not over-engineer it, just get
the comparison and measurement piece rock solid first.

If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn 
throughout the project. Try to leave the requirements in better shape than you found them.
Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.
Perhaps your current system is a shapeless mass of history and mystery like the one in Figure 21-2. 
Imagine that you’ve been asked to implement some new functionality in region A in this figure. 
Begin by recording the new requirements in a structured SRS or in a requirements management tool. 
When you add the new functionality, you’ll have to figure out how it interfaces to or fits in with the 
existing system. The bridges in Figure 21-2 between region A and your current system represent these 
interfaces. This analysis provides insight into the white portion of the current system, region B. In 
addition to the requirements for region A, this insight is the new knowledge you need to capture.CHAPTER 21 Enhancement and replacement projects 399

Rarely do you need to document the entire existing system. Focus detailed requirements efforts 
on the changes needed to meet the business objectives. If you’re replacing a system, start by 
documenting the areas prioritized as most important to achieve the business objectives or those that 
pose the highest implementation risk. Any new requirements identified during the gap analysis will 
need to be specified at the same level of precision and using the same techniques as you would for a 
new system.
Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

Most of this book describes requirements development as though you are beginning a new software

An enhancement project is one in which new capabilities are added to an existing system.

A replacement (or reengineering) project replaces an existing application with a new custom-built

- The tool lets a researcher open a pair of fingerprint files and view their minutiae points overlaid on the image.
- Clicking a point on one print and the matching point on the other calculates and displays the spatial deviation between them.
- Clicking an individual minutia shows its details: x/y position, angle, classification, and any annotations.
- Marking/filtering deviation pairs and exporting the filtered minutiae is a nice-to-have, not required for the first version.
- The core required flow is: open files, compare corresponding points, calculate deviation.
- A session can be saved as a session file that can be reopened later.
- A session can also be saved as a simple log file (table format, e.g. openable in Excel) listing the pairs and calculated deviations.
- The tool must work entirely offline and locally; it must not require any network or server communication.
- The intended users are biometrics researchers in academia, government labs, and industry, already familiar with minutiae and EBTS-type files.
- The interface does not need to be simplified for non-expert users.
- User accounts, per-user permissions, and security layers are explicitly out of scope.
- This is a prototype/beta-stage tool, not intended for general release or for ongoing developer support after delivery.

premissas: PA-01: Users already have prior familiarity with minutiae and EBTS-format files.
PA-02: [INFERRED] The tool runs as a local desktop utility, with no need for server installation.
restricoes: REST-01 (Scope): It is a prototype/beta-stage tool, not intended for general release nor for ongoing developer support after delivery.
REST-02 (Technical): The system must operate entirely offline and locally, with no dependency on network or server.

stakeholders.descricao: Biometrics researcher (academia, government labs, industry) — the sole user type, already familiar with minutiae and EBTS files; the interface does not need to be simplified for them.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The pair marking/filtering-by-deviation-threshold and filtered export feature is optional (nice-to-have) — only the open-compare-calculate flow is required for the first version.
The tool must operate entirely offline and locally — network or server communication is not permitted.
The interface does not need to be simplified for non-expert users — the target audience already understands minutiae and EBTS files.
User accounts, per-user permissions, and security layers are explicitly out of scope.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow the researcher to open a pair of fingerprint files.
The system must display each fingerprint image with its minutiae points overlaid.
The system must allow the researcher to click a point on one print and the corresponding point on the other print.
The system must calculate and display the spatial deviation between two selected corresponding minutiae points.
The system must allow the researcher to click an individual minutia and view its details (x/y position, angle, classification, annotations).
The system must allow the researcher to save the current session as a session file that can be reopened later.
The system must allow the researcher to save the session as a table-format log file (e.g., openable in Excel), listing the compared pairs and calculated deviations.
The system must allow the researcher to mark/filter deviation pairs by a threshold entered during the session — optional, nice-to-have (see RN-001).
The system must allow the researcher to export, to a new file, only the minutiae that pass the threshold filter — optional, nice-to-have (see RN-001).

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must operate entirely offline and locally, without requiring any network or server communication.
requisitos_nao_funcionais.metrica_aceitacao: All core functions (open, compare, save) work with the network disconnected

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The tool, even at prototype/beta stage, must be stable enough for an experienced researcher to rely on it without ongoing developer support after delivery.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a biometrics researcher, I want to open a pair of fingerprint files, so that I can compare their minutiae.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to see minutiae points overlaid on the images, so that I can visually identify corresponding points.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to click matching points on both prints and see the calculated spatial deviation, so that I can objectively measure how much the minutiae drifted between captures.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to click an individual minutia and see its details, so that I can inspect it closely.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to save my session and reopen it later, so that I can continue my work without losing progress.
As a biometrics researcher, I want to export a log with the compared pairs and deviations, so that I can analyze the results in a spreadsheet.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Compare fingerprint pair — the researcher opens two files, views the overlaid minutiae, selects corresponding points, and the system calculates and displays the deviation.
Save and resume session — the researcher saves the current session to a file and reopens it later to continue the work.
Export comparison log — the researcher exports a table-format log with all compared pairs and their deviations.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given two fingerprint files open with minutiae overlaid, when the researcher clicks a point on each print, then the system calculates and displays the spatial deviation between them.
Given a selected minutia point, when the researcher clicks it, then the system displays its x/y position, angle, classification, and any annotations.
Given an active session, when the researcher saves it as a session file, then the session can later be reopened with all prior comparisons intact.
Given a completed session, when the researcher exports the log, then the file lists all compared pairs and their calculated deviations in a table format openable in a spreadsheet.
Given the tool is running with no network connection, when the researcher performs any core operation (open, compare, save), then the tool functions normally without requiring network access.
